intro: Lightning Ridge is an opal-mining town in the far north-west of New South Wales, near the Queensland border, known for its black opal. A few kilometres south of it, in open bush among prickly pear, grows an old coolibah with a massive hollow trunk and limbs that sweep almost to the ground. A reader sent us its photograph and puts it at 500 years old.

trees.story:
A reader sent us this coolibah from the bush a few kilometres south of Lightning Ridge, the opal town of north-western New South Wales. They put it at 500 years old, with a question mark, and its trunk at 7.5 metres round. Those are their figures, not a measurement we have seen.

The photograph shows why they stopped. A man stands against the trunk, and the tree makes him small. The trunk is short and massive, with a dark hollow low on one side, and almost at once it throws out great grey limbs in every direction. Some climb into an airy crown of narrow blue-green leaves; others sweep down and out so far that one bends nearly to the ground before turning up again. Around it is open country of grass, saltbush and prickly pear.

The coolibah is the eucalypt of the inland floodplains, the tree under which the swagman camps in Waltzing Matilda. Its wood is hard and its trunks often grow hollow, which makes them difficult to date.

We do not know who owns the ground it stands on. If you know this tree, its name or its history, tell us here.
trees.how_to_recognise: Alone in open bush among prickly pear: a short, massive grey trunk with a dark hollow low on one side, its long limbs sweeping out so far that one bends almost to the ground.
trees.access: The reader walked up to it in open bush about five kilometres south of the town. We have not confirmed who owns the land; ask locally before you go.
